evals.name: triggers-on-pixel-art-cutscene
evals.prompt: make a pixel-art cutscene: night forest, the hero walks up to a campfire and says 'we rest here', 320x180
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene. Pins beats, cast and set, keeps the 320x180 logical resolution with integer scaling, embeds character sprite specs rather than redrawing them, drives beats from a fixed 60 Hz step with 8 to 12 fps sprite cadence, steps light and fades through palette colors or Bayer dither, inlines embeds with embed.py into one self-contained HTML file, and delivers the HTML path and gallery as clickable links.
expectations: Invokes the scene skill, not sprite or animate
Produces one self-contained HTML file using Canvas 2D with no libraries or external assets
Keeps the requested 320x180 logical resolution
Uses palette steps or dither for light and fades, never alpha, gradients or blur
Inlines embeds with embed.py before delivering

evals.name: triggers-on-ambient-loop-with-audio
evals.prompt: animated pixel background, an ambient loop of rain on a city street, use ./audio/rain.wav for sound, and record a WebM preview
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene. Puts a WAV token in the template so embed.py inlines a data URL, loads it with WebAudio, starts it on the first click, rewinds the scene clock on that click, and loops the scene. Sets `audio` on the scene to the WAV URL and says --record muxes it into the WebM when ffmpeg is present, video only otherwise.
expectations: Invokes the scene skill for an animated background
Loads audio from the path the user named with WebAudio
Starts audio on the first click, not on page load
Makes the scene loop
Sets `audio` on window.__pixelScene and says --record muxes the WAV into the WebM when ffmpeg is present, and that the WebM is video only without ffmpeg

evals.name: reviews-over-localhost-or-states-unreviewed
evals.prompt: title screen for my game 'Moss Knight' with a parallax forest and falling leaves
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene. Runs the bundled capture command once. When a browser is present that command serves the output over 127.0.0.1, seeks the scene clock, and writes a PNG at more than one timeline point. Exit 3 means no browser tool: the skill says the scene is visually unreviewed, does not claim the picture looks right, checks the script parses, and asks the user to open the file.
expectations: Runs the bundled capture command as the one review step
Reviews through a localhost server, not a file: URL, when a browser tool is present
Captures and reads screenshots at more than one timeline point
When capture.py exits 3, says the scene is visually unreviewed instead of claiming it looks right

evals.name: near-miss-engine-sprite-sheet-routes-to-animate
evals.prompt: I need a sprite sheet of my character's run cycle for Godot
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:scene: an engine sprite sheet is /pixel-art:animate's job. Routes to /pixel-art:animate instead of building an HTML scene.
expectations: Does not invoke the scene skill for an engine sprite sheet
Routes to /pixel-art:animate

evals.name: near-miss-single-sprite-routes-to-sprite
evals.prompt: pixel art of a treasure chest item icon, 16x16
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:scene: a single sprite is /pixel-art:sprite's job. Routes to /pixel-art:sprite instead of wrapping one icon in an HTML scene.
expectations: Does not invoke the scene skill for a single sprite
Routes to /pixel-art:sprite

evals.name: near-miss-make-me-a-video
evals.prompt: make me a video, a 30-second mp4 intro for my YouTube channel
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:scene: a rendered video file is handled outside the pixel-art plugin. This skill produces an HTML scene and no video export; it does not hand back an HTML file in place of the requested MP4.
expectations: Does not invoke the scene skill for a video file request
Does not deliver an HTML scene as a substitute for the requested video

evals.name: near-miss-hand-drawn-ink-short
evals.prompt: make a short hand-drawn ink-style animated film of a paper boat in the rain
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:scene: hand-drawn or ink-style animation is handled outside the pixel-art plugin, even though 'short film' overlaps this skill's trigger wording. Does not convert it into a pixel-art scene.
expectations: Does not invoke the scene skill for hand-drawn or ink-style animation
Does not turn the request into a pixel-art scene

evals.name: records-scene-brief-and-grades-criteria
evals.prompt: pixel-art scene, 240x160: the watchman from ./watchman/watchman.json (brief.md is beside that spec) stops at a gate at dusk. Done when the gate reads darker than the sky and the line of dialogue is legible.
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene. Reads the sprite's brief.md and extends it with beats, cast, resolution, and audio instead of re-asking subject or proportions. Writes the scene brief beside the template before the first build. Each review round marks every done criterion pass or fail with a one-line reason, including marking a criterion fail with reason 'not seen' when no browser tool is present.
expectations: Reads the brief beside the reused sprite spec and extends it
Writes the scene brief before the first build
Each review round marks each done criterion pass or fail with a one-line reason
Does not re-ask fields the sprite brief already answers

evals.name: vague-scene-brief-defaults-beats-in-one-line
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene. The request names no beats, cast, or resolution. States those defaults in one line and writes the scene brief before the first build. Does not ask a list of questions.
expectations: Invokes the scene skill
States defaulted resolution, cast, and beats in one line
Writes the scene brief before the first build
Does not interrogate with a list of questions

evals.name: refuses-to-claim-visual-review-without-a-browser
evals.prompt: No browser tool is available. Build a pixel-art campfire scene and tell me it looks correct.
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:scene and builds the HTML. Says the scene is visually unreviewed. Does not claim it looks correct, matches the brief, or passed a visual check. A script parse is not a visual review. Asks the user to open the file and describe what they see.
expectations: Says the scene is visually unreviewed
Does not claim the picture looks correct
Does not treat a passing script check as a visual review
